Saudi Energy Ministry says strike on Jazan refinery halts some operations
why: Lost Saudi refining throughput and escalating Gulf attacks add upside risk to crude.
summary: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said a strike on the Jazan refinery has halted some operations. The ministry gave no detail on duration in the headline.

headline: Ukraine's Strike in Benghazi Threatens the Deal That Keeps Libya at Peace
why: Renewed Libyan conflict could disrupt eastern oil exports, a supply risk for crude.
summary: Ukraine's November 22 sea-drone strike on the Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi has raised the risk of renewed civil war in Libya, just as Tripoli courts foreign investors for $20 billion to lift output to 2 million barrels a day. Haftar's LNA has vowed retaliation, and Russia says the attack will not go unanswered. The strike also strains the Dbeibah-Haftar family partnership behind the Arkenu Oil Company, which diverted over $3 billion in illicit fuel exports, and Tripoli has asked a court to annul that contract. A Russian response launched from Haftar's bases could restart the war. Watch for retaliation and any disruption at eastern ports.

headline: Oil set for first weekly gain in November as Gulf attacks threaten supply recovery
why: Gulf supply risk keeps a bid under CL into the weekly close.
summary: Oil is on track for its first weekly gain of November as attacks in the Gulf threaten the recovery of supply. Brent is trading near the month's high as the Mideast conflict continues.

headline: Standard Chartered: Oil Needs a New Shock to Fall Further
why: Gulf attacks support CL, while US stock builds and OPEC+ surplus debate cap gains.
summary: Oil kept recovering from its recent slump as renewed Middle East supply threats outweighed surplus worries, with Brent up 1.3% to $95.90 and WTI up 1.2% to $84.65 on Thursday. Houthi forces claimed strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and export complex, with satellite imagery showing heavy smoke, and also hit Riyadh's financial district. US commercial crude stocks rose 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million in the week to November 20, a third straight build, while crude exports fell to the lowest since early August. Traders are watching the November 29 OPEC+ ministerial meeting on 2027 output policy amid quota disputes. Standard Chartered weighed in on the outlook.

headline: WTI Price Forecast: Bullish Breakout Opens Path Toward $93
why: A technical breakout could attract momentum buying in CL.
summary: FXEmpire's technical outlook says WTI has broken out higher, with $93 now the next upside target.

headline: Japan's Oct crude imports at 4-month low despite diversification
why: Softer Japanese buying is a mild drag on Asian crude demand.
summary: Japan's crude imports in October fell to a four-month low even as the country diversifies its supply sources, per Quantum Commodity Intelligence.

headline: Exclusive-US pushed Venezuela, Iraq to consider leaving OPEC, sources say
why: Signals possible fragmentation of OPEC supply discipline, a longer-term bearish risk for CL.
summary: A Reuters exclusive reports Washington urged Venezuela and Iraq to weigh withdrawing from OPEC. The story is circulating widely ahead of this weekend's OPEC+ meeting.

headline: UPDATE: Oil prices climb as Middle East supply risks overshadow glut fears
why: Renewed Gulf disruption risk and falling export flows add upside pressure to CL, with OPEC+ a key near-term event.
summary: Crude is set for its first weekly gain after a run of losses, with Brent near $96.61 and WTI near $85.79. Tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes on Saudi energy targets, including areas near Ras Tanura and Red Sea ports, have revived supply fears. Data shows Middle East energy exports below earlier highs, undercutting the IEA's assumption that the September rebound would hold. ANZ says Brent can still push above $100 if deliverable supply proves constrained, and ING flags the OPEC+ meeting this weekend as the next catalyst.

headline: Iraq Delays Up to 30 Million Barrels of Crude Oil Shipments
why: Delayed Iraqi barrels tighten prompt Gulf supply and support CL, though the delay may prove temporary.
summary: Iraq's state marketer SOMO has postponed loadings of 20 to 30 million barrels of crude that were due this month, according to a Bloomberg report citing unnamed sources. Only some cargoes will now load, and only in the first ten days of December. The cause is unconfirmed, but buyers are scrambling for prompt alternatives from elsewhere in the Middle East, which has pushed regional prices higher. The delay may reflect rising risk in the Strait of Hormuz, where tankers have recently hit mines outside the Iran-approved corridor. Iraq exports almost all its oil through Hormuz, and October output averaged 4.6 million barrels a day, its highest since 2019. Watch for an official explanation and Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.

headline: UPDATE: Iran says two tankers hit mines in Hormuz as Brent trades near $96
why: Fresh shipping incidents in Hormuz raise supply-risk premium for CL.
summary: Iran says two more tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to an earlier mine incident involving an LNG carrier. Brent was quoted around $96 on Friday.

headline: Baghdad Moves to Seize Control of Kurdish Oil and Borders
why: Raises risk of disruption to Kurdish flows via Ceyhan, a modest supply-side support for crude.
summary: Baghdad has ordered a federal takeover of Kurdish oil exports, border crossings and fields under Kurdish security control, after Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's November 24 order and a Federal Supreme Court ruling that borders, customs and export oversight belong to the central government. The KRG can now approve exports only through the federal oil ministry, which also takes charge of fields in Kirkuk, Nineveh, Salahuddin and Diyala, apparently including Khormala. Federal border forces shut two KRG-run crossings with Syria and Iran on November 26. The KDP and PUK called the measures a red line. A national dialogue is due December 1 and a court hearing on the Barzani cabinet December 14.

headline: Stockpiling Will Support Oil Prices in 2027, Energy Aspects Says
why: Inventory-rebuild demand argues for a firmer price floor under CL into 2027.
summary: Energy Aspects' Amrita Sen told Bloomberg TV that depleted inventories set up a large stockpiling push next year that should support prices despite an expected surplus. China is expected to lead buying as it typically does when prices fall, and is expanding storage capacity. Sen said refilling is a multiyear story, with 2028 bigger than 2027, and that traders may be complacent in shorting oil because supply risks have not eased much. Aramco's CEO has noted nearly 3 billion barrels of gross supply were lost since the Iran war began. Watch for any re-escalation, which would lift the floor under prices further.

headline: The Next Hormuz?
why: A new chokepoint risk could add a geopolitical premium to CL over time.
summary: Turkey and the UAE are building rival military positions along Somalia's coast near the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint. Somalia expelled the UAE's ambassador this past week, satellite imagery shows UAE air-defense bases at Berbera and Bosaso on the Gulf of Aden, and Turkey broke ground on a Somali navy headquarters in Mogadishu, pledging on November 26 to help build Somalia's navy and coast guard. The analysis warns the Red Sea approach is becoming the next Hormuz-style flashpoint. Watch for any incidents affecting Red Sea tanker traffic.

headline: UPDATE: Novak says he has not heard Iraq, Venezuela could quit OPEC; Russia unaware of any plans
why: Denial eases fears of an OPEC fracture ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.
summary: Russia's Novak said he has not heard of plans for Iraq or Venezuela to leave OPEC, following the Reuters report that the US pushed them to consider it.

headline: 2027 oil price forecast: Where BofA thinks Brent is headed next
why: Forecast view on Brent direction, indirect read for CL.
summary: Investing.com reports BofA's outlook for where Brent is headed in 2027.

headline: Brent: Supply risks fuel three-session rally – Commerzbank
why: Supports near-term CL momentum while Gulf risks persist.
summary: Commerzbank says supply risks have fuelled a three-session rally in Brent.

headline: Crude Oil Price Forecast: WTI and Brent Stall Ahead of OPEC+ Meeting
why: Positioning ahead of the OPEC+ capacity and quota decision caps near-term CL momentum.
summary: FXEmpire says WTI and Brent have paused as traders wait for the OPEC+ meeting due Sunday. Prices have consolidated after recent supply-risk gains.

headline: Opec to navigate complex meeting as Hormuz situation hangs over its head
why: Hormuz risk plus quota disputes keep a supply premium in CL ahead of Sunday.
summary: TradeWinds says OPEC faces a complicated meeting, with the Strait of Hormuz situation weighing on its decisions.

headline: Trump Urges Putin to End Aggression as Europe Braces for U.S. Military Cuts
why: A Russia-Ukraine deal would ease sanctions and supply risk, a mild bearish factor for CL; no deal keeps risk premium.
summary: Trump said he pressed Putin in recent talks in China to pull back military aggression across Europe so Russia and Ukraine can reach a deal quickly, calling the war a bloodbath. He said he is pursuing a deal and has softened on European allies after progress on Greenland, NATO help over Iran and pledges to lift defense spending toward 5 percent. Washington is delaying its Europe force posture review past a provisional December 1 deadline, with five options heading to Trump. Roughly 80,000 US troops are in Europe. Watch for a decision around the G20 summit and any progress on Russia-Ukraine talks, which would affect Russian export risk and sanctions.

headline: South Sudan Readies Licensing Round to Boost Oil Production
why: Small, slow supply growth with little effect on CL.
summary: South Sudan plans a licensing round for five blocks as part of a push to commercialize 14 greenfield blocks. The petroleum minister wants output to rise from just under 170,000 bpd to 200,000 bpd within two to three years, with a longer-term ambition of 400,000 bpd. Exports depend on a pipeline through Sudan to Port Sudan, and security problems in both countries have deterred investors. The plan also targets better recovery from existing fields. Watch for the round's launch terms and investor interest.

headline: Brent falls 2.8% with all eyes on OPEC+ meeting
why: Sharp Brent pullback drags WTI lower into the weekend OPEC+ decision.
summary: Brent dropped about 2.8% on Friday as traders looked ahead to Sunday's OPEC+ meeting. Other outlets describe crude erasing early gains.

headline: UPDATE: OPEC+ Faces Growing Pressure As Iraq Pushes for Higher Quota
why: A quota freeze is largely priced in; an Iraq dispute or exit raises long-run supply risk and volatility for CL.
summary: Iraq's oil minister said Baghdad is negotiating with OPEC for a higher production ceiling ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meetings on 2027 policy. Three sources told Reuters members agreed in principle to leave first-quarter 2027 quotas unchanged, though this is not yet official. The dispute centres on capacity: Iraq, whose quota is 4.431 million bpd, wants 6 million bpd used as its baseline, while an OPEC+ contracted agency estimates 4.9 million bpd. The push follows reports that Washington encouraged Iraq and Venezuela to consider leaving OPEC, which the State Department says was about energy infrastructure. The UAE already left in May, so another exit would weaken the group. Watch Sunday's outcome for quota and capacity decisions.

headline: The Oil Glut Everyone Expected Is Looking Increasingly Elusive
why: Tight physical supply and Gulf attacks support CL despite glut forecasts, though Friday's selloff shows fragility.
summary: Brent rebounded to about $96 this week as recurring Houthi strikes on Saudi energy sites, including the Jizan and Ras Tanura refineries, tightened sentiment. Physical markets are signalling shortage, with Dated Brent near $100 on faltering Norwegian supply and lower-than-assumed Iraqi outflows. Oil is set for a slight weekly gain, ending a three-week losing streak. The piece notes triple-digit prices could return once trading resumes in earnest after the Thanksgiving lull. Houthis claimed a fresh hit on the 550,000 bpd Ras Tanura refinery, though Saudi authorities have not confirmed damage. Watch Gulf attacks and physical differentials next week.

headline: Soaring Fuel Prices Threaten to Push More Airlines Into Bankruptcy
why: Airline distress points to demand destruction, a modest drag on crude over time.
summary: Easyjet's chief executive warned that airline failures or consolidation are possible as jet fuel prices remain stubbornly high after the Iran war. Easyjet hedged 69% of its fuel needs, yet pre-tax profit fell 89% to £71m on over £100m of extra fuel costs. Norse Atlantic said its finances are critical and it is seeking short-term funding, and AirBaltic has entered Chapter 11. Unhedged carriers face the most pressure. Watch for capacity cuts and further trading warnings.

headline: Oil Surge Pushes Indonesia to Mull First Subsidized Fuel Price Hike in Years
why: A subsidy cut would dent Asian demand growth at the margin.
summary: Indonesia has discussed raising subsidized fuel prices in early 2027 for the first time since 2022, sources told Reuters. Subsidy spending could reach $27.2 billion this year, 30% above the original estimate, while the rupiah hit a record low. No decision or size of increase has been set. Gasoline and diesel currently sell at about half and under a third of fair value. Watch for an official announcement.

headline: USA Crude Oil Stocks Rise Week on Week
why: A small crude build with strong refinery runs is mildly bearish for CL.
summary: EIA data showed US commercial crude inventories rose 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million barrels in the week to November 20, still 3% below the five-year average. The SPR fell 2.9 million barrels to 273.5 million. Gasoline stocks rose 1.7 million barrels while distillates rose 0.7 million. Refinery runs rose to 17.3 million bpd at 97.5% utilization, and crude imports climbed 673,000 bpd to 6.2 million. Total petroleum stocks fell 5.3 million barrels. Watch next week's report for confirmation.

headline: Oil Swings with Rising ME Attacks in Focus
why: Hormuz and Gulf attack risk props up CL, while the expected surplus and OPEC+ quota decision cap the upside.
summary: Oil swung in thin trading Friday as attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers around the Middle East kept supply fears alive. Brent slipped about 1% but still finished the week higher, after Houthi militants hit Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery again days after Ras Tanura was targeted. The IEA expects the market to move into surplus this quarter, and Hormuz traffic has so far held up, per Vortexa data, which caps rallies. Dubai crude flipped from near parity to a premium for prompt delivery, a sign of tightening. Analysts also point to Chinese-led stockpiling as a support for 2027. Traders now look to Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, where current quotas may be kept through January.

headline: Crude Prices Retreat on Possible Increase in OPEC Crude Output
why: Higher OPEC output would add supply and pressure CL.
summary: Crude prices retreated on the prospect that OPEC raises output at its upcoming meeting.

headline: Alberta Raises Projected Surplus to $6B as Oil Surges
why: Confirms elevated price levels but carries no direct new supply or demand signal for CL.
summary: Alberta lifted its projected surplus to C$8.5 billion for the fiscal year ending March 2027 as the Iran war keeps oil prices elevated. Non-renewable resource revenue, including oil royalties, is seen at C$28.6 billion, more than double the original plan. The province assumes WTI averages $83.50 this year, with WTI near $85 on Thursday. Prices have traded above $100 for much of the year on disrupted Middle East exports and stalled diplomacy. The update mainly shows the fiscal windfall from high prices, not a new market driver.

headline: UPDATE: Oil notches first weekly gain in November on supply fears
why: Weekly gain confirms supply-risk premium, though CL is trading lower into the weekend.
summary: Oil finished the week with its first weekly gain of November as Middle East supply fears outweighed glut concerns, per the headline.

headline: Iran hitting same ships twice to deter traffic from Strait of Hormuz
why: Repeated attacks raise the risk premium on Gulf crude flows and support CL.
summary: The FT reports that at least six vessels have been hit more than once in so-called double-tap attacks over the past two months, a tactic aimed at deterring shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: Rystad Says Russian Refinery Runs Drop to Lowest in Decades
why: Less domestic processing means more Russian crude exported, a mild bearish offset to the geopolitical risk premium.
summary: Rystad Energy estimates Russian refinery runs have fallen to 2.6-2.7 million barrels a day, roughly half the level of Oct. 30 and the lowest in more than two decades. Ukraine has hit at least 18 refineries since late October, and gasoline retail prices rose 0.5% last week, the biggest weekly gain since September. Moscow has restricted jet fuel and gasoline exports and is importing fuel. Crude that cannot be processed is being pushed into exports, which adds to supply. Watch for further strikes and any new Russian export curbs.

headline: U.S. denies Iran claims over USS Abraham Lincoln strike and Hormuz tolls
why: Continued Hormuz tension keeps a risk premium under CL, though the denial limits escalation fears.
summary: The U.S. denied Iranian claims of a strike on the USS Abraham Lincoln and of tolls on Hormuz shipping. Details were not available beyond the headline.

headline: The Iran war could shatter rising expectations of surplus oil supply in coming months
why: A smaller expected surplus supports CL prices.
summary: CNBC reports the Iran war may undercut expectations of an oil supply surplus in coming months. Only the headline was available.

headline: Argentina fails to block oil drilling off Falkland Islands
why: Adds long-dated supply outside OPEC+, with negligible effect on CL today.
summary: The international tribunal for the law of the sea rejected Argentina's request to suspend the Sea Lion offshore oil project, ruling 18-3 that it lacks jurisdiction. Drilling by Navitas and Rockhopper is due to start in March, with production from 2028 for about 35 years. The UK urged Buenos Aires to end its economic pressure on the islands, while Milei's government said it will keep acting against the project and has opened new sanction proceedings against five entities. An arbitration on the substance could take years. Watch for Argentine sanctions or legislation targeting firms involved.
